NUTRITION
  ENERGY:
    - Moderate calorie deficit: target 10-15% below maintenance calories, minimum 1400 kcal/day.
  MACROS:
    - Protein: 1.6-2.0g/kg bodyweight per day.
    - Carbohydrate: 40-45% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, lentils, beans, quinoa, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables).
    - Fat: 25-30% of total calories, focus on unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish).
  MEAL STRUCTURE:
    - 3 main meals + 1-2 snacks per day.
    - Distribute carbohydrates evenly across meals to avoid large postprandial glucose spikes.
    - Include protein and fiber at every meal.
    - Avoid added sugars and minimize refined carbohydrates.
    - Hydration: at least 2L water per day.
  CHEAT_MEAL:
    - Allow 1 cheat meal per week, ideally at lunch.
    - Keep portion moderate and avoid deep-fried or very high-sugar foods.
    - Monitor blood glucose 1-2 hours after the cheat meal.
    - Resume regular eating pattern at next meal.
    - Do not skip meals before or after to "compensate."
    - If possible, include protein and vegetables in the cheat meal to help glycaemic control.
  SPECIAL_CONSIDERATIONS:
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after exercise, especially when increasing intensity or duration.
    - Carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
    - Coordinate meal timing with metformin dosing as per medical advice.
    - Prioritize non-starchy vegetables for volume and satiety.
    - Limit alcohol and avoid sugar-sweetened beverages.
    - For fasted cardio, monitor for hypoglycaemia and break fast if symptoms occur.
  PRE_WORKOUT_FASTED_CARDIO:
    - If truly fasted, no breakfast before cardio. Monitor blood glucose before starting.
    - If blood glucose is <5.5 mmol/L or if she feels at risk of hypoglycaemia, have a small snack:
      - Option 1: 1 small apple + 10g almonds
      - Option 2: 1 slice whole grain toast + 1 tsp natural peanut butter
      - Option 3: 100g low-fat plain Greek yogurt + 1/4 cup berries
    - After cardio, have a balanced breakfast:
      - Example: 2 eggs scrambled with spinach + 1 slice whole grain toast + 1/2 avocado
      - Example: 150g low-fat Greek yogurt + 30g oats + 1/2 banana + cinnamon
    - Avoid high-sugar foods and fruit juices before fasted cardio.
    - Always carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
  POST_WORKOUT_SNACKS:
    - 150g low-fat Greek yogurt + 1/4 cup berries
    - 1 small apple + 15g almonds
    - 1 slice whole grain bread + 2 tbsp cottage cheese
    - 1 boiled egg + 1 small orange
    - 100g low-fat cottage cheese + 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes
    - 1 small banana + 1 tbsp natural peanut butter
    - 1 protein shake (whey or plant-based, unsweetened) mixed with water
    - 1/2 cup hummus + raw carrot sticks
    - 1 small can tuna in water + 2 whole grain crackers
    - 1 cup low-sodium vegetable soup + 1 slice whole grain toast
  INTERMITTENT_FASTING:
    - Intermittent fasting (IF) can be considered, but must be approached with caution for type 2 diabetes.
    - Recommended protocol: 12:12 or 14:10 (e.g. eating window 7am–7pm or 8am–6pm).
    - Avoid prolonged fasting (>16 hours) unless cleared by her physician.
    - Do not skip meals if taking metformin or if prone to hypoglycaemia.
    - Always monitor blood glucose during fasting, especially when starting IF or increasing exercise.
    - Break the fast immediately if symptoms of hypoglycaemia occur (shakiness, sweating, confusion).
    - Meals during eating window should follow the prescribed macronutrient and calorie guidelines.
    - Hydration: water, black coffee, and unsweetened tea are allowed during fasting window.
    - No sugar-sweetened beverages or fruit juice during fasting.
    - Coordinate IF schedule with exercise and medication timing as per medical advice.
    - If using fasted cardio, ensure blood glucose is monitored and break fast if needed for safety.
    - Consult with her healthcare provider before starting or modifying any fasting protocol.

    - Hydration: at least 2L water per day.

  ENERGY:
    - Moderate calorie deficit: target 10-15% below maintenance calories, minimum 1400 kcal/day.
  MACROS:
    - Protein: 1.6-2.0g/kg bodyweight per day.
    - Carbohydrate: 40-45% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, lentils, beans, quinoa, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables).
    - Fat: 25-30% of total calories, focus on unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish).
  MEAL STRUCTURE:
    - 3 main meals + 1-2 snacks per day.
    - Distribute carbohydrates evenly across meals to avoid large postprandial glucose spikes.
    - Include protein and fiber at every meal.
    - Avoid added sugars and minimize refined carbohydrates.
    - Hydration: at least 2L water per day.
  SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS:
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after exercise, especially when increasing intensity or duration.
    - Carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
    - Coordinate meal timing with metformin dosing as per medical advice.
    - Prioritize non-starchy vegetables for volume and satiety.
    - Limit alcohol and avoid sugar-sweetened beverages.
    - For fasted cardio, monitor for hypoglycaemia and break fast if symptoms occur.

NUTRITION
  ENERGY:
    - Moderate calorie deficit: target 10-15% below maintenance calories, minimum 1400 kcal/day.
  MACROS:
    - Protein: 1.6-2.0g/kg bodyweight per day.
    - Carbohydrate: 40-45% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, lentils, beans, quinoa, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables).
    - Fat: 25-30% of total calories, focus on unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish).
  MEAL STRUCTURE:
    - 3 main meals + 1-2 snacks per day.
    - Distribute carbohydrates evenly across meals to avoid large postprandial glucose spikes.
    - Include protein and fiber at every meal.
    - Avoid added sugars and minimize refined carbohydrates.
    - Hydration: at least 2L water per day.
  CHEAT_MEAL:
    - Allow 1 cheat meal per week, ideally at lunch.
    - Keep portion moderate and avoid deep-fried or very high-sugar foods.
    - Monitor blood glucose 1-2 hours after the cheat meal.
    - Resume regular eating pattern at next meal.
    - Do not skip meals before or after to "compensate."
    - If possible, include protein and vegetables in the cheat meal to help glycaemic control.
  SPECIAL_CONSIDERATIONS:
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after exercise, especially when increasing intensity or duration.
    - Carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
    - Coordinate meal timing with metformin dosing as per medical advice.
    - Prioritize non-starchy vegetables for volume and satiety.
    - Limit alcohol and avoid sugar-sweetened beverages.
    - For fasted cardio, monitor for hypoglycaemia and break fast if symptoms occur.
  PRE_WORKOUT_FASTED_CARDIO:
    - If truly fasted, no breakfast before cardio. Monitor blood glucose before starting.
    - If blood glucose is <5.5 mmol/L or if she feels at risk of hypoglycaemia, have a small snack:
      - Option 1: 1 small apple + 10g almonds
      - Option 2: 1 slice whole grain toast + 1 tsp natural peanut butter
      - Option 3: 100g low-fat plain Greek yogurt + 1/4 cup berries
    - After cardio, have a balanced breakfast:
      - Example: 2 eggs scrambled with spinach + 1 slice whole grain toast + 1/2 avocado
      - Example: 150g low-fat Greek yogurt + 30g oats + 1/2 banana + cinnamon
    - Avoid high-sugar foods and fruit juices before fasted cardio.
    - Always carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
  POST_WORKOUT_SNACKS:
    - 150g low-fat Greek yogurt + 1/4 cup berries
    - 1 small apple + 15g almonds
    - 1 slice whole grain bread + 2 tbsp cottage cheese
    - 1 boiled egg + 1 small orange
    - 100g low-fat cottage cheese + 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes
    - 1 small banana + 1 tbsp natural peanut butter
    - 1 protein shake (whey or plant-based, unsweetened) mixed with water
    - 1/2 cup hummus + raw carrot sticks
    - 1 small can tuna in water + 2 whole grain crackers
    - 1 cup low-sodium vegetable soup + 1 slice whole grain toast
  INTERMITTENT_FASTING:
    - Intermittent fasting (IF) can be considered, but must be approached with caution for type 2 diabetes.
    - Recommended protocol: 12:12 or 14:10 (e.g. eating window 7am–7pm or 8am–6pm).
    - Avoid prolonged fasting (>16 hours) unless cleared by her physician.
    - Do not skip meals if taking metformin or if prone to hypoglycaemia.
    - Always monitor blood glucose during fasting, especially when starting IF or increasing exercise.
    - Break the fast immediately if symptoms of hypoglycaemia occur (shakiness, sweating, confusion).
    - Meals during eating window should follow the prescribed macronutrient and calorie guidelines.
    - Hydration: water, black coffee, and unsweetened tea are allowed during fasting window.
    - No sugar-sweetened beverages or fruit juice during fasting.
    - Coordinate IF schedule with exercise and medication timing as per medical advice.
    - If using fasted cardio, ensure blood glucose is monitored and break fast if needed for safety.
    - Consult with her healthcare provider before starting or modifying any fasting protocol.

NUTRITION
  ENERGY:
    - Moderate calorie deficit: target 10-15% below maintenance calories, minimum 1400 kcal/day.
  MACROS:
    - Protein: 1.6-2.0g/kg bodyweight per day.
    - Carbohydrate: 40-45% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, lentils, beans, quinoa, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables).
    - Fat: 25-30% of total calories, focus on unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish).
  MEAL STRUCTURE:
    - 3 main meals + 1-2 snacks per day.
    - Distribute carbohydrates evenly across meals to avoid large postprandial glucose spikes.
    - Include protein and fiber at every meal.
    - Avoid added sugars and minimize refined carbohydrates.
    - Hydration: at least 2L water per day.
  CHEAT_MEAL:
    - Allow 1 cheat meal per week, ideally at lunch.
    - Keep portion moderate and avoid deep-fried or very high-sugar foods.
    - Monitor blood glucose 1-2 hours after the cheat meal.
    - Resume regular eating pattern at next meal.
    - Do not skip meals before or after to "compensate."
    - If possible, include protein and vegetables in the cheat meal to help glycaemic control.
  SPECIAL_CONSIDERATIONS:
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after exercise, especially when increasing intensity or duration.
    - Carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
    - Coordinate meal timing with metformin dosing as per medical advice.
    - Prioritize non-starchy vegetables for volume and satiety.
    - Limit alcohol and avoid sugar-sweetened beverages.
    - For fasted cardio, monitor for hypoglycaemia and break fast if symptoms occur.
  PRE_WORKOUT_FASTED_CARDIO:
    - If truly fasted, no breakfast before cardio. Monitor blood glucose before starting.
    - If blood glucose is <5.5 mmol/L or if she feels at risk of hypoglycaemia, have a small snack:
      - Option 1: 1 small apple + 10g almonds
      - Option 2: 1 slice whole grain toast + 1 tsp natural peanut butter
      - Option 3: 100g low-fat plain Greek yogurt + 1/4 cup berries
    - After cardio, have a balanced breakfast:
      - Example: 2 eggs scrambled with spinach + 1 slice whole grain toast + 1/2 avocado
      - Example: 150g low-fat Greek yogurt + 30g oats + 1/2 banana + cinnamon
    - Avoid high-sugar foods and fruit juices before fasted cardio.
    - Always carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
  POST_WORKOUT_SNACKS:
    - 150g low-fat Greek yogurt + 1/4 cup berries
    - 1 small apple + 15g almonds
    - 1 slice whole grain bread + 2 tbsp cottage cheese
    - 1 boiled egg + 1 small orange
    - 100g low-fat cottage cheese + 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes
    - 1 small banana + 1 tbsp natural peanut butter
    - 1 protein shake (whey or plant-based, unsweetened) mixed with water
    - 1/2 cup hummus + raw carrot sticks
    - 1 small can tuna in water + 2 whole grain crackers
    - 1 cup low-sodium vegetable soup + 1 slice whole grain toast
  INTERMITTENT_FASTING:
    - Intermittent fasting (IF) can be considered, but must be approached with caution for type 2 diabetes.
    - Recommended protocol: 12:12 or 14:10 (e.g. eating window 7am–7pm or 8am–6pm).
    - Avoid prolonged fasting (>16 hours) unless cleared by her physician.
    - Do not skip meals if taking metformin or if prone to hypoglycaemia.
    - Always monitor blood glucose during fasting, especially when starting IF or increasing exercise.
    - Break the fast immediately if symptoms of hypoglycaemia occur (shakiness, sweating, confusion).
    - Meals during eating window should follow the prescribed macronutrient and calorie guidelines.
    - Hydration: water, black coffee, and unsweetened tea are allowed during fasting window.
    - No sugar-sweetened beverages or fruit juice during fasting.
    - Coordinate IF schedule with exercise and medication timing as per medical advice.
    - If using fasted cardio, ensure blood glucose is monitored and break fast if needed for safety.
    - Consult with her healthcare provider before starting or modifying any fasting protocol.
